blocks.text: COTABATO CITY – Environment officials in North Cotabato province released an adult Philippine serpent eagle (Spilornis holospilus) into the wild on Tuesday after receiving medical clearance from local authorities. Maria Elvira Lumayag, regional executive director of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Region 12 (DENR-12), said the raptor was first rescued on Nov. 16 by a vigilant resident in Barangay Midpapan, Pigcawayan, North Cotabato, and immediately surrendered to the Municipal Environment and Natural Resources Office (MENRO). From an initial check-up with Pigcawayan’s municipal veterinarian, the eagle was transferred to the Community Environment and Natural Resources Office in Midsayap town […]...
